The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file's own driller-training beat is elsewhere.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:2 depth:6 start:25,25
steps.description: depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: spacing tightened from 5m to 2m to keep this 9-hole grid's drilling time reasonable for a single driller/drill_rig (no staffed:true near-origin spawn on a campaign map).
#553: drain the ordered plan in bounded 50-tick chunks -- each chunk is followed by `event choose 0` since a `tick` command stops dead the instant a timer event fires mid-block (events.ts).
Sixth and final chunk — all 9 holes should have landed by now.

#581: the command said `contract accept 1`, and contract #1 is not on offer at this point in EITHER mode -- both dump the available pool as ids 4-11, so the command was silently accepting nothing (`activeContractCount` stayed 0 right through it) and the `contract deliver 4` guard below was operating on a contract nothing had accepted. Interaction mode was the half that worked: the unscoped click landed on the first offered card, which IS #4, which is why that guard finds #4's active card and correctly reports its DELIVER disabled. So the click was right and the command text was wrong; the command now names #4 and the click is scoped to it. Nothing downstream is re-baselined -- the three steps after the guard are `observe` and assert nothing.

BLOCKED, and deliberately not converted to a click: nothing is in storage at this point, so ContractsPanel disables the amount box, MAX and DELIVER together (maxDeliverable = min(remaining, stored) is 0). The console command is no better -- it returns success:false and command mode only fails a step on a thrown exception, so this step is a silent no-op in both modes. Two modes genuinely disagree on WHY, and that is worth knowing: in command mode `contract accept 1` above fails outright ("Contract #1 not found or already completed") -- by this point in the campaign, `generateContracts`' CONTRACT_REFRESH_INTERVAL cycling has already carried ids past 1, confirmed directly (`contract list` at this exact point offers [4, 5, ...], not 1) -- leaving activeContractCount at 0 and no card at all, while the interaction-mode click on `.bs-contract-accept` accepts whichever contract is really on offer (the array's first entry, id 4, matching render()'s insertion order). So no `equals` is asserted here -- only `expect.blocked`, which is interaction-mode-only and therefore checks the mode where a card actually exists, scoped to id 4 to match what actually gets accepted rather than the stale id 1 an earlier campaign-length change left behind.
